initialText.title: Task 1
initialText.text:
Match each message (1-5) and its meaning (A-F). There is one letter that you do not need. There is an example at the beginning (0→G).

0 When you come to London, there’s no need for you to book into a hotel. You can sleep at my place.
1 I’m afraid you’ll get angry with me, but I have to tell you what happened. I’ve broken your new iPad, and I can’t afford to have it fixed. I feel terrible.
2 We all know that you had good intentions, but we all make mistakes sometimes. Just apologise sincerely, explain yourself, learn from it and move on. Beating yourself up won’t help anyone.
3 The tea is in the pot, and there’s plenty of fruit in the fridge. Stay in bed and take both aspirins and vitamins regularly. You should feel better soon.
4 Handling this machine is a bit risky and should be done properly, so read the instructions carefully and make sure everybody listens and wears all the protective gear that came in the package.
5 Moving out of your comfort zone will require a bit of courage and confidence. Life is sometimes scary, but playing it safe is not how you achieve great things.

A Don’t feel bad.
B Be careful.
C It’s repaired.
D Take the risk.
E I am so sorry.
F Take care of yourself.
G Stay with me.

initialText.title: Heyside Hall
initialText.text: Heyside Hall was completed in 1831 and designed by David Welby. Construction was carried out by John Platt. Epwick is ten minutes away, Bailden about twenty and Baschester half an hour away. Heyside Hall shows the neo-Gothic style. It has 570 windows.

Task 3
      Questions 11-15

      You will hear a radio interview with Rav Gupta, a tennis coach, about children in sports.
      For each question (11-15), choose the correct answer (A, B or C).
      You will hear the recording twice.


 11     How long has Rav worked as a tennis coach?

        A For two years.
        B For three years.
        C For ten years.



 12     Why do children play sports, according to Rav?

        A They feel enjoyment.
        B Their parents make them.
        C They like winning.



 13     When should children start practising sports, according to Rav?

        A As early as possible.
        B When they are motivated.
        C After they start attending school.



 14     Who influenced Rav’s final choice of sport?

        A His father.
        B His teacher.
        C His friend.



 15     What negative role do parents play in children’s sports, according to Rav?

        A They pressure them too much.
        B They don’t support their children.

           B It wasn’t difficult because she had practised before.
           C It got less difficult after more time spent hiking.
